I would keep to the wheat-maize rotation this year. In Quzhou County, that is the steadiest way for me to use my land, water, labor, and machinery. I am 60, so I would not choose a crop that needs too much hand work or too much market gambling. Winter wheat and summer maize fit my habits and the local climate, and I know how to manage them well enough without making the year too complicated. I would use improved or hybrid seed, put most of the fertilizer into wheat and maize because those are the crops that give me the safest grain yield, and keep field work simple with ploughing before wheat and rotary tillage before maize. I would irrigate wheat more than maize, because wheat in our area usually needs more careful water management. I would also keep pesticide use moderate, only enough to protect yield, because spending too much raises my cost and does not always bring back more grain.
